test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they do not confirm to real world knowledge, decide which of the given conclusions / possibilities can be true on the basis of the statements.

**Statements:**

1. All greens are reds.

2. Some reds are browns.

3. All greys are browns.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some greys are greens.

II. All browns are reds is a possibility.

III. Some browns are greens.

options.text: Only conclusion I and II are true

solution:
Given Statements:

1. All greens are reds.

2. Some reds are browns.

3. All greys are browns.

The least possible diagram: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c50e52b40c205424afc7c74bef95711bad92fe72f10fb1e6ab0ea5295b66eb8.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some greys are greens. - False (Because, there is no direct relative between greys and greens.)

II. All browns are reds is a possibility. - True (Because, Some reds are browns so All browns can be reds)

III. Some browns are greens. - False (Because, there is no direct relative between browns and greens.)

So, Only conclusion II is true.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**
